subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is the replacement character defined by <Picture 1>.

<Picture 1> contains multiple views of the same single character.
The front view, side view, and rear view all represent one consistent identity.

Use all views together to preserve:
facial identity,
facial proportions,
hairstyle,
hair volume,
body proportions,
the off-shoulder white outfit,
black bow decoration,
corset lacing,
black lace trim,
sleeve structure,
fabric details,
colors,
materials,
and all distinctive appearance features.

Do not interpret the multiple views in <Picture 1> as multiple people.

<Video 1> is a hybrid structural editing reference.

The normal RGB regions of <Video 1> define the original source scene and must be preserved as strongly as possible, including:
the dark nighttime alley,
industrial corridor,
walls,
doors,
background structures,
red neon lighting,
cool blue lighting,
street lights,
ground,
perspective,
camera position,
camera framing,
camera movement,
depth relationships,
lighting direction,
shadow structure,
and temporal structure.

Do not redesign, clean up, simplify, brighten, or replace the original environment.

The grayscale depth-rendered region corresponds exclusively to the tracked foreground speaking subject selected for replacement.

The grayscale depth region is not appearance information.

Do not reproduce:
grayscale color,
depth-map shading,
black contour,
dark halo,
mask boundary,
or depth texture.

Use the depth-rendered subject strictly as structural and motion guidance for:
body position,
silhouette,
3D volume,
body orientation,
head position,
head rotation,
head movement,
mouth movement,
speaking motion,
facial motion,
eye direction,
neck movement,
shoulder movement,
arm position,
hand position,
hand gesture,
finger direction,
upper-body movement,
gesture timing,
spatial position,
depth ordering,
and temporal motion.

summary:

[single-character replacement + speaking performance + hand-gesture preservation + strict depth-guided reconstruction + source-scene preservation]

Replace only the tracked foreground subject represented by the depth-rendered region in <Video 1> with <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>.

The replacement character must strictly follow the original tracked subject's:
body position,
body orientation,
scale,
perspective,
head pose,
head movement,
mouth movement,
speaking rhythm,
facial motion,
eye direction,
arm motion,
hand position,
hand gesture,
finger direction,
upper-body motion,
spatial placement,
and timing.

The hand gestures are important motion information.
Preserve the original timing, direction, height, reach, and spatial relationship of the hands and arms as closely as possible.

The replacement character should appear naturally present inside the original nighttime alley and should inherit the original scene lighting.

Preserve the red and blue environmental lighting on the character naturally while retaining the identity and outfit defined by <Picture 1>.

Preserve all normal RGB regions of <Video 1> as strongly as possible.

Do not modify:
the alley,
walls,
doors,
background structures,
lights,
ground,
camera framing,
camera movement,
perspective,
or scene timing.

The grayscale depth representation must completely disappear and be replaced by the fully rendered <Subject 1>.

Avoid:
original subject identity,
original male facial identity,
original hairstyle,
original black jacket identity,
identity drift,
face instability,
hairstyle changes,
outfit changes,
costume simplification,
character duplication,
extra people,
merged anatomy,
duplicated arms,
duplicated hands,
missing fingers,
broken hands,
incorrect finger direction,
incorrect hand position,
incorrect mouth motion,
incorrect speaking rhythm,
grayscale depth texture,
black outlines,
dark halos,
visible mask boundaries,
background deformation,
environment redesign,
lighting replacement,
camera changes,
and unintended scene changes.

subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is the replacement character defined by <Picture 1>.

<Picture 1> contains multiple views of the same single female character.
The front view, side view, and rear view all represent one consistent identity.

Use all views together to preserve:
the same facial identity,
silver-gray long hair,
hair length and volume,
facial proportions,
body proportions,
white fitted sleeveless top,
black outer garment,
necklace,
skin tone,
clothing structure,
colors,
materials,
and all distinctive appearance details.

Do not interpret the multiple views in <Picture 1> as multiple people.

<Video 1> is the primary motion and structural reference.

The normal RGB regions of <Video 1> define the source scene and must be preserved as strongly as possible, including:
the blue studio background,
the floor,
the original lighting,
the camera position,
the fixed camera framing,
the perspective,
the lower-left Chinese title graphic,
and the temporal structure.

The grayscale depth-rendered human region in <Video 1> corresponds exclusively to the tracked performer.

The depth-rendered region is authoritative structural and motion guidance.

Do not treat the grayscale depth region as appearance information.

Do not reproduce:
grayscale color,
depth-map shading,
black contours,
dark halos,
mask boundaries,
or depth texture.

motion_instruction:

<Subject 1> must strictly reproduce the full-body movement of the tracked performer in <Video 1>.

The motion is a rapid lateral dodge-step / sidestep demonstration.

The performer begins in a centered upright stance.

During the movement:
the body shifts rapidly sideways,
the feet separate into a wider stance,
the knees bend naturally,
the center of gravity moves laterally,
the torso leans slightly in the direction of movement,
the shoulders follow the body shift,
the arms move naturally for balance,
and the head remains coordinated with the body.

After reaching the lateral position,
the performer quickly recovers back toward the original centered stance.

Preserve the exact movement rhythm from <Video 1>.

If the source motion repeats,
reproduce each repetition with the same:
timing,
lateral travel distance,
foot placement,
stance width,
weight transfer,
torso lean,
arm counterbalance,
recovery speed,
and pause timing.

summary:

[character replacement + strict depth-guided full-body motion reconstruction + source-scene preservation]

Replace only the tracked depth-rendered performer in <Video 1> with <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>.

<Picture 1> determines who the character is.

<Video 1> and its depth-rendered human region determine exactly how the character moves.

Motion guidance from <Video 1> has priority over invented animation.

Strictly preserve:
body position,
full-body silhouette,
scale,
orientation,
foot trajectory,
foot contact with the floor,
leg spacing,
knee bending,
center-of-gravity movement,
torso lean,
shoulder motion,
arm motion,
head position,
lateral displacement,
acceleration,
deceleration,
recovery timing,
and frame-by-frame temporal motion.

The replacement character must remain visually consistent with <Picture 1> throughout the entire clip.

The long silver-gray hair and clothing may react naturally to the fast lateral movement,
but must not change the underlying motion trajectory.

Preserve the original blue studio scene as strongly as possible.

The camera remains fixed.
Do not add camera movement.
Do not redesign the environment.
Do not remove or alter the lower-left source graphic outside the tracked subject region.

The grayscale depth representation must completely disappear in the final result and be replaced by a fully rendered <Subject 1>.

avoid:

original performer identity,
original male appearance,
original clothing,
identity drift,
face instability,
hair color changes,
hair shortening,
hairstyle changes,
outfit changes,
character duplication,
extra people,
merged anatomy,
extra arms,
extra legs,
broken limbs,
incorrect foot placement,
foot sliding,
floating feet,
broken knees,
incorrect body balance,
incorrect lateral trajectory,
invented dance movements,
walking forward,
walking backward,
running,
jumping,
spinning,
punching,
speaking,
lip-sync motion,
unnecessary hand gestures,
slow-motion behavior,
motion exaggeration,
grayscale depth texture,
black outlines,
dark halos,
visible mask edges,
background reconstruction,
camera movement,
and unintended scene changes.
